title: Elevation scale with layered shadows
when: The user wants cards, menus, dialogs and sticky bars to look layered, or current shadows look muddy and inconsistent.
prompt:
Goal: Four or five elevation levels, each a shadow and z-index pair used by role, so depth means the same thing everywhere.
Steps:
1. Levels by role: 0 flat page, 1 raised cards, 2 dropdowns and popovers, 3 dialogs and drawers, 4 toasts.
2. Build each shadow from two layers, a tight contact one and a soft ambient one: --shadow-1: 0 1px 2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.06), 0 1px 3px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1); higher levels grow blur and offset, not opacity.
3. Tint shadows toward the background hue (a dark navy at low alpha) instead of pure black.
4. Pair each level with a z-index token (--z-dropdown 100, --z-sticky 200, --z-dialog 300, --z-toast 400); no raw numbers.
5. On dark themes show elevation with lighter surfaces and a subtle border.
6. Keep one light source: every shadow falls downward.
Quality bar:
- At most five shadow values in the stylesheet.
- Cards rise one level on hover, not three.
- No element with both a heavy border and a heavy shadow.
Pitfalls:
- z-index: 9999 wars.
- Single heavy shadows at 0.5 opacity.
- Shadows on everything, text included.
Verify:
- [ ] --shadow-0 to --shadow-4 on :root.
- [ ] z-index values use tokens.
- [ ] Components use shadow tokens only.
- [ ] Dark theme uses surface lightness.
Output: Elevation tokens on :root and component rules in style.css.

examples.input: as sombras do site estao pesadas e cada uma de um jeito
examples.output: shadow-1 cards, shadow-2 menus, shadow-3 dialog, two layer navy tinted, z tokens 100 to 400
